subject: Workplace Skills
title: Designing Your Workspace
description: A quick, practical guide to Designing Your Workspace.

hook.text: Working from the couch sounds great until your back hurts and your brain associates relaxation with deadlines.

buildup.text: Your brain ties locations to activities. If the bed is your office, sleep suffers and focus suffers.

discovery.text: A dedicated workspace — even a corner of a room — signals 'work mode' when you sit down and 'off' when you leave.

twist.text: You don't need a home office. A consistent spot with a closed door or noise-canceling headphones works fine.

climax.text: Invest in a good chair and decent lighting. Your body is in that spot eight hours a day. Treat it accordingly.

punchline.text: Same spot, same time, different mode. The space trains you.

quiz.question: Why is a dedicated workspace important for remote work?
options: It impresses colleagues during video calls
The brain ties locations to activities, separating work from rest
